original.reason: The conclusion is correct, but the exclusion argument omits the intervening term pq and falsely infers p∤m merely from m>p.

judgment.reason: It omits the interior term pq when claiming to classify every term strictly between p² and q².
The purported exhaustive square exclusion leaves out pq, which lies strictly between p² and q².
The statement that all interior terms have p<t<q omits pq, so the proof does not exclude every possible square.
Its classification of terms strictly between consecutive prime squares omits pq, leaving a material gap.
